## Proposed sector

Name the sector, domain, mission, or operating environment.

## Scope

Describe the systems and uses the module should cover.

## Why a separate overlay is needed

Explain which risks, authorities, operating conditions, or harms are not adequately addressed by the universal five-dimension review alone.

## Principal decisions or actions

Identify what AI systems in this sector may:

- decide;
- recommend;
- rank;
- predict;
- control;
- automate;
- deny;
- allocate;
- monitor;
- physically execute.

## Affected people, institutions, or missions

Identify who or what may be affected.

## Sector-specific risks

Address relevant risks such as:

- rights and civil liberties;
- safety;
- accessibility;
- discrimination;
- professional standards;
- operational resilience;
- cybersecurity;
- physical control;
- public accountability;
- mission failure;
- vendor or supply-chain dependency.

## Proposed review domains

List the sector-specific questions or control categories the module should contain.

## Proposed deployment blockers

List deficiencies that should presumptively prevent deployment or continued operation.

## Required evidence

Identify the documentation, testing, logs, validation, professional review, or authority needed for a defensible assessment.

## Applicable authorities and standards

List relevant statutes, regulations, directives, standards, professional guidance, or agency policies. Verify currency before relying on them.

## Interaction with existing overlays

Identify overlaps with existing modules, including:

- employment;
- lending;
- healthcare;
- government;
- telecommunications;
- defense and national security;
- NASA and space systems;
- critical infrastructure;
- biometrics;
- transportation;
- robotics;
- other modules.

## Evaluation cases

Provide at least two representative test scenarios:

1.
2.

## Checklist

- [ ] The proposal supplements rather than replaces the five universal dimensions.
- [ ] The scope is specific enough to avoid duplicating an existing module.
- [ ] Proposed blockers are tied to foreseeable harm.
- [ ] Required evidence is identified.
- [ ] At least two evaluation cases are included.
